page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized, network and EBS-optimized instance type built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled with a local 300 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the network baseline bandwidth is rated at 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6870.73 and a PassMark CPU score of 7626.07. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 382.09 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 51.32 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. However, single-core performance is weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1155.0 and a weak stress-ng single-core score of 1304.38. Database operations on PassMark are also weak at 2587.31, though Redis SET operations achieve an average of 6.38 million operations per second.

The r5dn.2xlarge offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads that require fast local storage, such as caching layers, in-memory databases, and search indexes. The inclusion of a 300 GB NVMe SSD and high network optimization provides qualitative cost efficiency by reducing the need for separate high-speed block storage attachments. However, users should note the weak single-threaded performance and poor medium-parameter LLM inference speeds, which make it less suitable for heavy compute-bound tasks or modern AI generation workloads.
